sources.entry: SensibleSideButtons - Small menu bar utility that lets you use your third-party mouse's side buttons for navigation across a variety of apps.

summary.one_liner: A small macOS menu bar utility that maps third-party mouse side buttons to 3-finger swipe gestures so they can navigate back and forward in almost any window.
summary.what_it_does: The README says macOS mostly ignores the M4/M5 side buttons on third-party mice, and that binding them to ⌘+[ and ⌘+] only works in a few apps. This tool instead makes the side buttons simulate 3-finger swipes, which lets them navigate almost any window that keeps a history. It runs from the menu bar. The README says the behavior was modeled on the Logitech MX Master. It also gives instructions for adding the app to Login Items so it starts at boot on macOS Ventura and later, and on Monterey and earlier. The README does not describe configuration options or the internal implementation.
use_cases: Back and forward navigation with a third-party mouse on macOS
Using mouse side buttons in browsers and other apps with history
Replacing unreliable ⌘+[ and ⌘+] shortcuts for mouse buttons
Making a Logitech-style side button work on a Mac
Launching a menu bar utility at login on macOS
how_to_run: Download or build SensibleSideButtons.app (the README does not give build commands)
Move SensibleSideButtons.app to Applications and open it
Add SensibleSideButtons.app under System Settings > General > Login Items > Open at Login to start it at boot
stack: Objective-C or Swift (not stated in README)
notable: Converts mouse side button presses into 3-finger swipe gestures, not key shortcuts
Works in almost any window with a navigation history, per the README
Modeled on the Logitech MX Master side button behavior
caveats: macOS only; the README describes macOS login item setup
The README points to external material for extensive information and gives no setup or configuration details
No license is named in the README
keywords: use mouse back button in any app
